findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/HopfAlgebra/Basic.lean:76 `export HopfAlgebraStruct (antipode)` and its docstring line 21 `HopfAlgebra.antipode`; Mathlib lemma statements use `HopfAlgebra.antipode` (MonoidAlgebra.lean:76, 82). In TauCeti, `grep -rn HopfAlgebraStruct TauCeti/` returns only `FiniteDual.lean:403-404` (instance head) and `:412` (a simp-unfold inside a proof), while public statements use `HopfAlgebra.antipode k (A := ...)` (FiniteDual.lean:410, SymmetricAlgebra/Basic.lean:82). findings.fix: Rename to `hopfAlgebraAntipode_eq_antipode` and state it as `HopfAlgebra.antipode R (A := U) = UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.antipode R`; update the `## Main declarations` entry at line 28.
findings.issue: `hopfAlgebraStructAntipode_eq_antipode` names the accessor by the internal carrier class `HopfAlgebraStruct`, not the canonical `HopfAlgebra.antipode`. Since the two are the same declaration (Mathlib `export HopfAlgebraStruct (antipode)`), the name invents a distinction that does not exist and is not what a user would grep for; the same name is advertised in the module docstring (line 28).

summary: Names and notation are otherwise consistent with the adjacent universal-enveloping and symmetric-algebra files; the sole public theorem is named after `HopfAlgebraStruct.antipode` instead of the canonical `HopfAlgebra.antipode` used everywhere else in Mathlib and TauCeti.
